app.title: GelAnnotate
app.summary: A person uploads a gel image, and the interface finds the lanes automatically or fits a regular comb when they type in the number of lanes they loaded. They correct lane centres in a table and type a label above and below each lane, with up to three more label rows underneath. They pick the molecular-weight standard they ran and the lane it is in; the interface finds that lane's bands and fits them to the stated sizes, and any band the gel did not resolve is placed from the fit. They adjust the title, fonts and display, then save or download the annotated figure at the format and resolution they choose.

task.text: Turn a raw gel image into a labelled, size-calibrated figure ready for publication.

data.text: One photographed or scanned image of a gel, a table of labels for each lane, and a preset list of reference sizes for the standard that was run.
data.item: a lane on a gel image

stage.text: labelling a finished gel image for a publication figure, after the gel is run and imaged

mechanism.text: Sidebar sections set the image, the lane detection, the standard and the appearance. Four tabs then hold editable tables (lane labels, lane centres, marker band rows) next to a figure preview, which redraws on every edit without detecting the lanes again. Two buttons run the automatic steps (detect lanes, find bands in the standard lane), and every value they produce can still be changed by hand.

field.text: lane and band annotation of electrophoresis gels in molecular biology

workflow.name: find the regions of an image, label each, calibrate a scale and export the figure

steps.here: Upload a gel image (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, or HEIC if available; 8- or 16-bit). Loading a new image clears the lanes, labels and markers.

steps.step: find the regions to annotate, then correct them by hand
steps.here: Lanes are found by picking peaks in the image's column profile. Entering the lane count fits a regular comb instead, and sliders crop the rows and columns searched. In the Lanes tab, centres can be nudged, added or deleted, and the changes applied.
A table with one row per lane has 'above' and 'below' text fields and up to three more rows for further tiers, with a live preview of the figure beside it.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Choose a standard from the presets (protein kDa, DNA bp, RNA nt, or custom) and the lane it was loaded into. 'Find bands in this lane' detects that lane's bands and fits them to the stated sizes with a log-linear mobility model, then reports how many bands matched and the r².

steps.step: correct the computed positions by hand
steps.here: The marker table lets each band's row be edited or hidden, and 'Place bands by hand' spreads every band between a top and a bottom anchor row.
Choose the title, caption, font size, label rotation and display options, then save to a path as PNG, TIFF, PDF, SVG or JPEG at a chosen dpi, or download a PNG.

distinctive: Typing the lane count fits a regular comb, so lanes with no sample still get a position, which the image alone cannot give.

Standard bands are matched to stated sizes by a robust pairwise fit, linear in log10(size). Extra peaks are ignored, unresolved bands are placed from the model and drawn dashed, and fewer than three matches or r² ≤ 0.99 triggers a warning.
Ladder presets carry a 'verified' flag, and the interface warns when a ladder's band values have not been checked against the vendor's documentation.
Labels come in tiers: one row above each lane and several rows below, for treatment, genotype or time point.
The input can be a phone photograph: sliders crop out the tray and background, and options set the band polarity, flatten uneven lighting and correct rotation.
